targets.authors: Muething C, Call N, Pavlov A, Ringdahl J, Gillespie S, Clark S, & Mevers JL
targets.title: Prevalence of renewal of problem behavior during context changes
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of the current investigation was to replicate the retrospective analysis described by Muething et al. (2020) .
targets.outcome_quote: Muething et al. (2020) found that renewal occurred in 45 of 67 (67%) cases. Similarly, renewal also occurred in the majority of cases within the current study (20 of 34 cases; 59%). Across 34 patients with 37 treatment evaluations, renewal occurred in 47 of the 200 context changes (24% overall) with renewal more likely following a person change (25%) than a setting change (17%; Figure 1 ). The overall identification of renewal effects across all context changes was lower in this data set than reported by Muething et al. (2020 ; 42% overall), but both estimates represent a sizeable proportion of patients.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors confirm renewal in a majority of cases, but explicitly report lower renewal prevalence across context changes. They additionally contrast the original decrease in magnitude with no significant magnitude/trend differences in the current data. No overriding whole-replication verdict.
